title: Benefit Interpretation: Medically Necessary Contact Lenses on Cascade Vision Plans
content:
**Benefit interpretation — Vision Plans**

**Rule.** Contact lenses are medically necessary only when the provider certifies one of the plan's qualifying conditions. These are keratoconus; anisometropia of 3 diopters or more; high ametropia of 10 diopters or more; and corrected acuity improvement not achievable with glasses.

Certified contact lenses are then:
- covered in full in network after the materials copay, where the plan covers medically necessary contacts in full in network; and
- reimbursed up to the plan's out-of-network medically necessary contact-lens amount out of network.

Without such a certification the contacts are elective. The member's own statement of a condition does not make them medically necessary. A plan that does not cover medically necessary contacts in network treats all contacts as not covered.

**Authority and record.** The certification is read from the contact-lens line of that claim: its contact-lens reason shows medically necessary or elective, and it is tied to the claim by the claim number. What the member says about a diagnosis does not change that reason.

| Provider certification on the claim | Plan covers medically necessary contacts in full in network | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Certified medically necessary | Yes | Covered in full in network after the materials copay; out of network up to the medically necessary amount |
| Not certified (member's statement only, or none) | Yes | Elective contact lenses |
| Either | No (not covered) | All contacts are not covered |
